_comment: klt erc supply spec for this block's merged GDS layout/comparator.gds -- the
supply read the T1 item 11 (structural power delivery) requires, per
klayout-tools docs/design-evidence-tiers.md item 11 and #56.
Run it against the committed GDS with:
klt erc layout/comparator.gds layout/erc-supply-spec.json \
--deck gf180mcu --format json > layout/erc/comparator.erc.json
(exit code 4 is the documented contract for this PDK: the antenna half
has no gf180mcu limit table yet, so that half rolls not_checked; the
connectivity half that item 11 grades is erc_status, see
docs/cli/erc.md's "Two verdicts" section. The committed report was
produced with klt 0.5.0+gb15edf5e3a2e, built from 2AMLogic/klayout-tools
commit b15edf5e -- the installed v0.5.0 release predates the erc
provenance/status envelope (klayout-tools#1984) that the item-11
content-hash requirement cites.)
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way:
- stackup[0] MUST carry role: "gate" (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2. active_layer Comp 22/0 narrows the gate area
to true poly-over-diff (klayout-tools docs/cli/erc.md "Gate area",
issue #1979) -- the salicide-blocked ppolyf_u_1k resistor bodies are
drawn on the same 30/0 layer as gates, and active_layer keeps their
area out of gates[].gate_area_um2.
- Metal1-Metal3 are the ONLY metals this block's supply is routed on:
route_nets.py's channel route puts trunks on Metal3, risers on Metal2,
and the tap pads / device-terminal escape stubs on Metal1. Verified
against the GDS rather than assumed: `klt layers layout/comparator.gds`
shows zero shapes on 46/0 (Metal4) and 81/0 (Metal5), so declaring
them would add two empty conductor regions. The item asks for a
stackup covering the layers the supply is routed on -- exactly these
three.
- label_layer 42/10 appears ONLY on Metal3, because that is the only
layer this block's merged GDS actually puts supply text on: the
router writes its per-trunk labels on 42/10 -- `vdd` and `vss` each
appear there twice (top and bottom trunks). Metal1's 34/10 text layer
exists in this GDS but carries only the `vinp`/`vinn` gen-compose
pins[] labels, so declaring 34/10 would add nothing to the supply
read. (The gf180mcuD 1_layer/10_label text datatype is the PDK's own,
taken from libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp at the pinned
open_pdks commit.)
- GDS layer numbers are gf180mcu's own drawn-layer numbers, derived
from the PDK's own lyp (variant gf180mcuC -- the 3.3 V variant this
block's layout work uses per layout/README.md's Toolchain notes;
open_pdks c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b at this host;
core-metal numbering is identical in the gf180mcuD lyp, also checked)
AND cross-checked against klayout-tools' curated gf180mcu deck layer
table -- Poly2 30/0, COMP 22/0, Contact 33/0, Metal1 34/0, Via1
35/0, Metal2 36/0, Via2 38/0, Metal3 42/0, Metal3_Label 42/10.
- nets[]: vdd and vss both kind: "supply", which is what makes a short
between them report as the severe erc.supply_short rather than the
general erc.multiply_driven_net. Each must resolve to exactly ONE
electrical island: erc.unconnected_net fires on zero matches (nothing
in the layout carries that label at all) AND on more than one (the
supply is split into pieces that never touch) -- so zero findings of
that rule naming either supply is exactly the 'one island per
supply' verdict, not merely an absence. The split-rail case is
precisely the failure mode this spec exists to detect.
- There is deliberately NO ties[] section, and that is a recorded gap,
not an oversight: klt erc's ties[] collapses a real routed design's
wells/taps into one electrical island and reports a FALSE
erc.supply_short (klayout-tools#2169, reproduced four ways in
gf180-drone-fc's FRICTION F-034 -- our fleet's worked example lands on
the same omission for the same reason). Because ties[] is omitted,
erc.missing_tie is NOT COMPUTED by this run -- the committed report
records that mechanically, as erc_coverage.inapplicable reason
`no_ties_declared` -- and its absence is an absence of evidence, not
evidence of absence. What does stand in for it: the well/substrate
taps the router itself draws -- route_nets.plant_taps() plants 6
Nwell taps tied up to `vdd` Metal1 pads plus 2 Pplus substrate ties
tied up to `vss`, joined into those nets as ordinary router pins;
comparator.routing.json totals.tap_pins=8 and the vdd/vss rows of
layout/README.md's generated routing table carry them, and
layout/lvs/comparator.extract.json extracts them as part of the named
vdd/vss nets. Those drawn ties are also why this PDK's extraction
deck resolves every PMOS body to `vdd` rather than to an anonymous
Nwell net (layout/README.md "Body ties are drawn here too").
- Run with --deck gf180mcu, and this is not decorative: the #2183
mirror artifact applies to this block. The two ppolyf_u_1k preamp
load resistors are drawn ON the declared gate-role layer -- their
bodies are Poly2 30/0 (salicide block 49/0, Resistor 62/0,
RES_MK 110/5; the curated deck's own comment records that a marked
poly segment "stays ordinary connected poly") and each spans from
its `aon`/`aop` terminal to its `vdd` terminal through that body.
A deviceless connectivity model therefore reads each body as a wire:
WITHOUT the carve-out, `vdd`'s one island swallows aon and aop
(a run without --deck literally reports gates[] net 'aon,aop,vdd').
--deck gf180mcu (klayout-tools#2217/#2205) subtracts the
deck-recognized resistor bodies from connectivity, echoing
ppolyf_u_1k on poly2 into provenance.devices exactly as a
hand-declared devices[] entry would be echoed -- the committed
report's one-island-per-supply verdict is the honest metal-only
read, with the carve-out machine-recorded rather than asserted.
